mechanism_narrative: The observed week-on-week increase in RETAIL_REC over the last four weeks indicates a sustained recovery trend that will continue, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as the city reopens.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the average of the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in PARKS mobility, having risen above the -30% threshold, indicates increased outdoor activity and willingness to leave home, which will spill over into retail and recreation, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility has risen above -30% from baseline
failure_condition: PARKS mobility remains above -30% but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: A combined and sustained increase in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility suggests a return to office-based work and associated commuting, which will directly increase foot traffic in retail and recreation areas during weekdays, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: Despite continued increases in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT, RETAIL_REC does not show a sustained increase over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: As the RESIDENTIAL mobility index continues its downward trend, indicating fewer people staying home, this sustained shift in behavior will free up more time for out-of-home activities, directly boosting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks, especially during the reopening phase.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility continues to decrease, but RETAIL_REC declines or stagnates over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained recovery in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, nearing the -30% baseline, indicates a broader comfort with public spaces and essential outings, which will translate into increased discretionary retail and recreation visits over the next one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM mobility rises above -30% from baseline
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM mobility rises above -30% but RETAIL_REC does not increase in the subsequent 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in PARKS mobility and decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility signifies a strong public desire and comfort with leaving home for leisure, which will positively influence RETAIL_REC as people seek more diverse out-of-home experiences over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: PARKS mobility increases while RESIDENTIAL mobility decreases, but RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent week-on-week increase in TRANSIT mobility reflects a gradual return to normal commuting and movement patterns, which is a leading indicator for increased foot traffic in retail and recreation areas, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility continues to increase, but RETAIL_REC fails to show a positive trend over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: As the city continues its phased reopening, the sustained increase in WORKPLACES mobility indicates more businesses are operating and employees are returning, creating a baseline level of activity that will support a rise in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks, provided reopening policies remain in effect.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility continues to increase, but RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 14 days, or if reopening policies are reversed.
